Market Maker Model (MMXM)

A broad campaign narrative describing price moving away from an origin range in stages, reaching a higher-timeframe reference area, and potentially reversing through prior ranges or pauses. The wording does not prove the actual orders or intentions of a market maker.

Open interactive ICT Academy →Official ICT channel ↗Official playlists ↗

How to identify and use this concept

  1. Mark the original consolidation or dealing range.
  2. Map the first directional leg and intermediate consolidations as price moves away from the origin.
  3. Identify a higher-timeframe reference area where a reversal would need separate confirmation.
  4. Only map the next leg after a clear structure/delivery shift; mark invalidation and opposing liquidity.
Use as a multi-leg narrative map during historical chart study, not as an intraday trigger by itself.

Common mistakes and limitations

Retrofitting every chart into a buy/sell campaign; treating “market maker” language as evidence of a specific institution; assuming the entire path must complete.
